title: Arsenio's style compared with Machito's groups
summary: Machito calls Arsenio unpolished but with flavor and fully black, while his own sextets were a half-breed music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I see. Okay, so then at that time in 1933 when you heard Arsenio, would you say that he was very advanced at that time period for where Cuban music was at?
No. We was too far advanced about what he was playing.
Yes, Agabama and the other guy and the other guy because - and then came this fellow.......
You were with Nacional for a while. Was he?
Ah - that was a different category completely.

Not that it was worst or better, nothing, he has his own style. He - a style that he could top up with - for his limitation. Harmonically he was not rich, so we was more advanced, musically, than Arsenio really was. He was more - uh - unpolished but with flavor. His music was more black that we was playing.
Let's say our music was a half-breed and his music was black.
From - - derived from the Congo where his parents came from?
